toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Sade begin' used intransitively like this reads as a calque of English 'seeds begin'; 'ontstaan' says the same thing idiomatically.
toegepas.fout: 'Nuwe sade begin' uses 'begin' intransitively for seeds in an English-like, vague way.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Ontstaan' is the natural Afrikaans verb for seeds coming into being and keeps the meaning exactly.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'daar binne-in' is clumsy; the adverb 'daarbinne' (one word) is the natural form here.
toegepas.fout: 'Daar binne-in' is clumsy and repeats 'binne-in' from the previous sentence.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Daarbinne' is the natural one-word adverb and says the same thing.

toegepas.blok: Wat die vrug en die saad doen
toegepas.voor: en los die sade ver weg
toegepas.na: en laat die sade ver weg agter
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'los die sade ver weg' is colloquial and unclear; 'laat ... agter' is the standard idiom for leaving something behind somewhere.
toegepas.fout: 'Los die sade ver weg' is colloquial and could be misread ('los' as loose).
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Laat die sade ver weg agter' is the standard idiom for the same action, with the same actors and place.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Onkruid' is normally a collective noun, so 'n onkruid' reads oddly; 'n onkruidplant' names a single plant naturally.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'n Onkruid' for a single weed plant is accepted, natural Afrikaans; 'onkruidplant' is heavier for a Grade 4 reader and only reads differently.

laat_vaar.voor: suig ook water uit die grond op vir die plant
laat_vaar.na: suig ook water vir die plant uit die grond op
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans the separable particle 'op' closes the clause; 'vir die plant' after it reads as a tacked-on afterthought.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Placing 'vir die plant' after the particle 'op' is normal, natural Afrikaans word order, so the reordering is a lateral move.

na_skrywer.voor: Die deel wat water na die blare dra
na_skrywer.na: Die deel van 'n plant wat water na die blare dra
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: A glossary entry is read on its own, so 'Die deel' needs to say what it is a part of; this may touch a shared definition, so the reviewer may prefer to route it.
na_skrywer.fout: The glossary entry opens with 'Die deel' without saying what it is a part of, which is unclear when the entry is read on its own.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The point is real, but this is a shared glossary definition and rewording it beyond spelling or grammar belongs to the writer.
